text:
jin: Observed weird memory growth on long-context Qwen-MQA runs this morning. KV hit rate drops after ~8k tokens and eviction churn spikes, even though sequence length distribution hasn't changed. Attaching quick profiler dump below and a short repro note.

tara: Can you paste the top counters and which kernel variant was chosen by the runtime?

jin: Kernel chosen: `mqa_fastpath_v2` on A100c. Batch heuristic config: `continuous_batch_max=32`, `batch_merge_time_ms=8`. Key counters: 
```
kv_pages_alloc = 12384
kv_pages_in_use = 11102
kv_page_faults = 3892
kv_evictions = 2721
kv_reuse_hits = 804 (drops dramatically after 7800 tokens)
rope_scale = 1.25
```
Notice `kv_pages_alloc` climbs linearly during longprefix traces.

alex: Hm. That looks like index aliasing rather than pure leak. When rope_scale > 1 we do bucket remapping for speed; if our page-to-bucket hashing uses 32-bit offsets we can get wraparound with MQA's slot packing. Could result in pages being treated as distinct and not matched to existing cache entries -> fragmentation + phantom allocations.

eli: Do we have a short repro? If so try forcing `gqa_fallback` kernel or temporarily disable compacting GC to see whether the growth stops. That narrows kernel vs GC.

jin: Minimal repro command I'm using: `pytest tests/perf/test_kv_longcontext.py::test_qwen_mqa_growth -k longprefix -q --runslow`. Quick tail of the run log: 
```
[00:00:45] seq=4000 tokens, kv_pages_alloc=6400, evictions=120
[00:02:10] seq=8200 tokens, kv_pages_alloc=12384, evictions=1210
[00:04:35] seq=12000 tokens, kv_pages_alloc=18456, evictions=2718
```
So allocations keep growing as if reuse matching is failing.

perf-bot: Perf alert created: PERF-4821. Regression: +12% memory vs baseline for qwen-mqa longprefix canonical. See /perf/alerts/4821.

tara: Another angle: our batching heuristic sometimes merges requests that are mid-rope-step with earlier in-flight requests; that can increase effective per-GPU live KV working set because merged batches pin pages longer. If kernel selects packing layout based on batch composition, merge + rope scale can blow up fragmentation. Suggest instrumenting `kv_page_owner` and `kv_page_bucket` mapping and capture samples around the 7.5k-9k token window.

alex: I'll add a lightweight sampling probe (1% samples) to dump bucket ids and owner lifetimes; also plan to run a canary with `continuous_batch_max=16` + `mqa_fastpath_v1` to see if packing/pin time changes. If probe shows repeated alternate-bucket allocations for same logical key, that's our bug.

jin: Starting canary now on canary-rt-14. Will attach probe output when done. cc @eli to coordinate kernel toggles during the run.

eli: On it :thumbsup: I'll prepare a non-compacting GC build to test isolate GC effect. If that stabilizes reuse, we know compaction + packing interaction is the root.

jin: Thanks — will update thread with probe dumps. Short term mitigation: lowering `continuous_batch_max` to 16 for Qwen-MQA routes in routing policy.

tara: Nice triage plan. If we confirm, we should also add an assert in the bucket remap path that validates that logical keys map consistently across rope_scale changes to catch regressions in CI.

alex: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up PR with the probe + assertion if canary repros.

jin: Appendix: small snippet of probe expectation format (will include full dump in follow-up):
```
{timestamp: 4812345700, worker: 3, logical_key: 0x7f9a1, bucket_id: 0x2a9, page_id: 0x10f3, owner_epoch: 42}
{timestamp: 4812345725, worker: 3, logical_key: 0x7f9a1, bucket_id: 0x3b2, page_id: 0x11ff, owner_epoch: 43}
```
If the same `logical_key` maps to different `bucket_id` in short succession that's the suspicious signal.

perf-bot: Linked issue: GITHUB-REDWOOD/INF-1599 (kv bucket remap sanity checks).

eli: Cool — I'll run the non-compacting GC test after the canary finishes (estimate ~2h).

jin: Thanks everyone. I'll post results here when canary completes. :coffee:
